nearest_existing_cases.relationship: These are direct DO SQL prepared/cursor/transaction-view/schema-cache behaviors, not public D1 binding objects, wire row shapes, sessions or D1 metadata. Their substantive overlap is recorded per candidate; none are relabeled or recounted.

Raw cursor iteration, typed SQL cursor BLOB binds, direct root scope isolation and connection-delta characterization are nearby concepts; new cases use materially different public D1 request/result contracts and do not claim cursor/concurrency coverage.

source_example: The source D1 guestbook uses ordinary exec/prepare/bind/run/first/all but has no assertion-bearing corpus case IDs. New cases are not copies of its GET/POST workflow.
limits: Search only the restored available text corpus; private/omitted tests may exist.
No claim these are the first D1 tests globally; independent review must decide distinct accepted credit.
No restored corpus mutation or duplicate case credit.

E203.distinction: D212 binds native SQL scalars and DataView and returns native ArrayBuffer; E203 exercises public D1 boolean normalization, JSON transport, SQL null and typed scalar persistence across batch/read dispatches.

E204.distinction: D212 observes a native DataView byte window and ArrayBuffer output. E204 tests the independently implemented D1 bind serializer: Uint16Array/Int8Array element truncation and typed-source copying at bind, then JSON byte-array output. Those are different encoding rules, not a new byte sample.

E205.distinction: D214 exhausts a native SQL RETURNING cursor and checks terminality. E205 compares public D1 run/all method aliases, success/result envelopes and RETURNING on both, with no exposed cursor.

E209.distinction: D213 has the same outward last-duplicate versus positional contract on native SqlStorageCursor paths. E209 independently targets D1 __d1Shape/Object.fromEntries and public raw/first/all across engine JSON rows. This is the closest cross-wave semantic overlap; independent review must decide whether separate public-surface implementation coverage merits distinct credit.

E212.distinction: D216/D217 use sql.ingest with remainder/rowsWritten/statementCount. E212 targets the separate D1 SQLite tail walker, public count/duration-only envelope, comments and a complete final statement without semicolon, then post-return committed contents. It makes no ingest or streaming-suffix claim.

E213.distinction: D219 drains read SELECT rows in sql.ingest before later writes. E213 uses public D1 exec(rows:false) with both multirow INSERT RETURNING and UPDATE RETURNING and checks all effects after its successful transaction-completing response plus no public results field.

E216.distinction: D214 explicitly drains all native cursor receipts; E216 asks D1 first() to retain one receipt while the engine must still step the entire mutation. A native cursor completion test does not exercise that keep=1 boundary.

current_sibling_wave_audited.credit_qualification: Naming a separate public API is not by itself a distinctness proof; independent review decides accepted credit, especially E209/D213.
